Job Description:

Analyze regulatory changes, assess operational impacts, and recommend compliance strategies.
Represent TWG in government or industry committees.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives in safety performance, environmental stewardship, and operational efficiency.
Ensure timely completion of activities and tasks assigned through the company EHS Management System (Intelex).
Work with management teams to identify, develop, and implement continuous improvement projects applicable to both regulatory and operational improvements.
Analyze, interpret, and understand laws and regulations enacted by State, Local, and Federal Agencies, its impact on company’s operations and provide recommendations to implement lawful and cost-effective compliance.
Gather in-field data from multiple facilities and compile into one central location.

Serve as a highly skilled technical expert responsible for the safe, efficient operation, maintenance, troubleshooting, and optimization of industrial ammonia refrigeration systems and HVAC equipment used for precise wine and juice temperature control, as well as facility climate management. The Refrigeration/HVAC Technician will perform advanced diagnostics, repairs, and preventive maintenance on ammonia-based central systems (including compressors, condensers, evaporators, vessels, valves, pumps, and controls) and HVAC components (such as chillers, air handlers, rooftop units, and ductwork). In the absence of the Sr. Ref/HVAC Tech, assume supervisory responsibilities for daily HVAC/refrigeration operations, ensuring compliance with all safety protocols (including PSM/RMP for ammonia), company SOPs, and regulatory standards (OSHA, EPA). Maintain product integrity, promote energy efficiency, and drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance system reliability, reduce downtime, and minimize costs/waste.
 
They will also help in the administration of company, department rules, regulations, and standard operating procedures. The technician will be held accountable in maintaining product integrity and creating safe an efficient production flow according to TWG protocols.
 
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
 

Expertly operate, monitor, troubleshoot, repair, and maintain industrial ammonia refrigeration systems, ensuring optimal performance for wine/juice temperature control while adhering to Process Safety Management (PSM) and Risk Management Program (RMP) requirements.
Diagnose and resolve complex mechanical, electrical, and control issues in ammonia systems (e.g., screw/reciprocal compressors, evaporative condensers, glycol/brine loops) and HVAC systems (e.g., package units, split systems, chilled water loops).
Perform preventive and predictive maintenance, including inspections, oil analysis, vibration monitoring, leak detection/repair, valve overhauls, pump-outs, and system pump-downs/restarts, following all mandated safety procedures.
Complete accurate documentation, including logs, maintenance records, work orders, PSM checklists, and regulatory compliance reports.
Demonstrate strong leadership: train and mentor team members on refrigeration/HVAC processes, safety protocols, and SOPs; assign workloads and evaluate performance when acting in a supervisory capacity.
Analyze operational data to identify inefficiencies, recommend improvements (e.g., energy-saving upgrades, process optimizations), and proactively address potential issues to prevent downtime or quality impacts.
Interact effectively with management, vendors, contractors, and cross-functional teams; communicate technical information clearly in verbal and written form.
Ensure full compliance with all company policies, safety standards, GMPs, OSHA/EPA regulations, and winery-specific protocols for hazardous chemical handling (including ammonia).

 
OTHER FUNCTIONS
 

Support emergency response and participate in incident investigations related to refrigeration/HVAC systems.
Assist with system installations, modifications, or upgrades as needed.
Model The Wine Group core values in all decisions and actions.

Support and model all company procedures and policies.

QUALIFICATIONS
 

Minimum 4 - 5 + years of hands-on experience with industrial ammonia refrigeration systems (preferred in food/beverage/winery environments) and demonstrated expertise in HVAC maintenance/repair.
Proven advanced knowledge of ammonia refrigeration principles, components, and troubleshooting (e.g., screw/reciprocating compressors, electrical controls, PLCs, alarm systems).
Experience with HVAC systems, including chillers, air conditioning units, ventilation, and related utilities.

Excellent computer skills (Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook; familiarity with CMMS or refrigeration monitoring software a plus).
Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and initiative in fast-paced environments.
Superior attention to detail, safety record, attendance, and work performance history.
